topicName: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussians Splatting

[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Modern 3D Computer Vision"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"Recent advancements in computer vision and computer graphics have fundamentally shifted how we represent 3D scenes. Traditional mesh-based representations are being replaced by volumetric and point-based continuous representations. This tutorial covers the theory and practical implications of Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) Fundamentals"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"NeRF represents a continuous 3D scene as a neural network, typically a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP). The input to the network is a 3D spatial coordinate (x, y, z) and a viewing direction (theta, phi). The output is the volume density (sigma) and view-dependent RGB color (r, g, b)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Input: 3D coordinates and 2D viewing directions."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Model: Multilayer Perceptron with positional encoding."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Output: Volume density and emitted color for ray marching."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"NeRF Rendering Equation"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"To render a pixel, NeRF casts a ray from the camera center through the pixel and samples points along the ray. It then applies volume rendering to accumulate color and opacity:"},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"def volume_rendering(rgb_samples, density_samples, ray_deltas):
    # Standard alpha blending along a ray
    one_minus_alpha = torch.exp(-density_samples * ray_deltas)
    alpha = 1.0 - one_minus_alpha
    weights = alpha * torch.cumprod(torch.cat([torch.ones((1,), device=alpha.device), one_minus_alpha[:-1]], dim=0), dim=0)
    color = torch.sum(weights.unsqueeze(-1) * rgb_samples, dim=0)
    return color"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Transitioning to 3D Gaussian Splatting"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"While NeRFs produce photorealistic results, they suffer from slow rendering speeds due to dense ray marching. 3D Gaussian Splatting solves this by replacing neural implicit fields with explicit 3D Gaussians, enabling real-time rendering at high resolutions."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Explicit Representation: Scenes are modeled using millions of anisotropic 3D Gaussians."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Parameters per Gaussian: Mean position, covariance matrix (scaling and rotation), opacity, and spherical harmonics coefficients for view-dependent color."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Rasterization: Instead of ray marching, 3D Gaussians are projected onto the 2D image plane (splatted) and alpha-blended."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Comparative Summary"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"NeRFs are ideal for memory-efficient storage and optimization without explicit structure, but are computationally expensive at inference time. 3D Gaussian Splatting trades off storage space for massive rendering speedups, making it the preferred choice for interactive applications, AR, and VR."}]
